amendments.normalized_body: In `nitrogen_cycle.rs` lines 131-134, the `.max(0.0)` clamps on `(don_consumed_mg - live_biomass_nitrogen_mg(decomp_growth, n_to_c)).max(0.0)` and the equivalent carbon line silently swallow tiny negative values from floating-point rounding in `constrained_live_growth_g`. While the constraint function prevents meaningful overruns, repeated rounding over long simulations could accumulate a drift that the 1e-6 guard tolerance masks. Consider asserting via `debug_assert!` that the pre-clamp value is >= some small negative threshold (e.g., -1e-9) so that a logic error in `constrained_live_growth_g` doesn't silently leak mass.

The `test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields` structural coverage test relies on naming conventions (`*_mg_n_total`, `*_mg_c_total`, `*biomass_g`, etc.) to auto-discover budget-relevant fields. If a future pool uses a non-standard name (e.g., `organic_sludge_mg` instead of `organic_sludge_g_total`), it will silently escape the coverage check. The doc-comments on `nitrogen_budget_components` and `carbon_budget_components` mention this risk but provide no compile-time or CI enforcement. Consider adding a `#[deny(unused)]` marker attribute or a manual registry pattern that forces new TankState fields to explicitly opt in or out of budget tracking.

The `SiphonDetritus` action is classified as open-system in `is_open_system_action_label` but has no dedicated budget tracking test verifying that the exported mass is properly recorded as an explicit export in the ledger (unlike `WaterChangePercent` which has `test_water_change_n_export_tracked`). Add a test analogous to `test_water_change_n_export_tracked` that siphons detritus, verifies total N/C decreased by the expected amount, and confirms the budget ledger entry shows the export as an explicit outflow rather than unexplained loss.

`crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:58-63` and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/chemistry.rs:314-329` now normalize non-finite carbonate-solver outcomes to an interior `pH 7.0`, and both `crates/tank_core/src/types/source_water.rs:66-75` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:75-89` treat that result as a valid source-water profile. That is a validation regression: a profile such as `dic_mg_c_per_l = 1e308, alkalinity_meq_per_l = 1.0` currently passes validation even though the quadratic has overflowed internally. The old preset-side validation rejected non-finite solves instead of collapsing them to neutral water. Please preserve an explicit error path when the shared solver had to use the non-finite neutral fallback, rather than accepting those inputs as calibrated source water.
